title: The wine's price label
hook: Would the same wine taste different under a different displayed price?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Separate an expectation-induced rating difference from a change in the liquid.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Separate an expectation-induced rating difference from a change in the liquid.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy sample keeps liquid identifier one while its label changes from €10 to €90. How much did the price label change? Toy inputs A=[10, 90, 1, 1]; B=[10, 10, 1, 1].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[80, 1, 1], [0, 1, 1]]. Labels: Label change €, Liquid before, Liquid after.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The label manipulation is visible while the liquid identifier remains fixed. An expectation-induced rating difference would be a separate outcome. This model does not transform a price tag into a physical change in the wine.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Old label €=10, New label €=10, Liquid id before=1, Liquid id after=1. What is Label change €? Answer: 0.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Old label €=10, New label €=10, Liquid id before=1, Liquid id after=1. What is Label change €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: The same wine labeled $90 rather than $10 was rated more pleasant, and reward-related brain activity rose with it (Plassmann, O'Doherty, Shiv & Rangel, 2008).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Separate an expectation-induced rating difference from a change in the liquid.
